content.text:
`urllib.parse.urlsplit()` is the function that splits a URL into five components, and `urllib.parse.urlunsplit()` reverses it.

The corpus describes `urlunsplit` as combining the elements of a tuple returned by `urlsplit` into a complete URL string. Its `parts` argument can be any five-item iterable. The result may be a slightly different but equivalent URL if the original had redundant parts. I did not read the `urlsplit` entry itself, so the five-component count comes from the `urlunsplit` description.

Source: `library/urllib.parse.rst`

```json
{"facts": {"split": "urlsplit", "join": "urlunsplit"}}
```
